item.title: Nationalist Party backs a basic salary for artists
item.description: Opposition leader Alex Borg said the Nationalist Party supports MEIAs proposal for a basic publicly funded salary for artists, made at a party-organised discussion on low pay, lack of recognition and limited access to cultural spaces. MEIA had proposed a defined, time-limited pilot giving regular income to professional artists in the run-up to the budget speech. The move follows comments by Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea that drew an angry reaction from artists and demands for his resignation; the minister has since said he will work to regain the sectors trust.

item.title: Foreign workers called to take part in week-long protest against Budget 2027
item.description: TCN Alliance Malta has launched the Green Ribbon Project, calling on third-country nationals to boycott public transport and shops from Monday, stay at home on Friday and end the week with a protest concert in Valletta against Budget 2027 measures. Patricia Garam said the campaign is a peaceful but undeniable confrontation with policies that pushed workers to a breaking point. The group said some foreign workers are reluctant to take part publicly because they fear possible repercussions.

item.title: Local plans must change, Abela says, as he acknowledges population concerns
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela said Maltas local plans must be revised because the framework introduced in 2006 has left a sour taste, insisting he has a strong mandate to take difficult decisions on planning. Speaking to journalists from Malta Daily, Lovin Malta and Whos Who, he acknowledged public concerns about population growth and pressure on schools and hospitals from foreign workers, saying the country needs foreign labour but not in excessive numbers. He also said the population report drafted by Finance Minister Clyde Caruana in 2018 does not form part of Cabinet records, so he cannot publish a document he does not hold, and advised those wanting it to approach its author.

item.title: Miriam Dalli reappointed as EU co-negotiator on climate adaptation at COP31
item.description: Minister for Energy, Environment and the Regeneration of the Grand Harbour Miriam Dalli will represent the European Union at COP31 in Antalya as co-negotiator on climate change adaptation, alongside the Dutch Minister. Ireland, which currently holds the Council Presidency, made the announcement. Dalli held the same EU role at COP28 in Dubai and COP29 in Baku, and said small island states such as Malta face particular challenges from rising temperatures, water scarcity and extreme weather.

item.title: Young victim of Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq boat incident undergoes successful surgery
item.description: Ben Caruana Rizzo, 14, who was found unconscious after a boat ran aground on a reef off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq a week ago, underwent successful surgery on Sunday. His father Keith Caruana, 48, died in the same incident, while a third man, Daniel Buttigieg, came out of a coma a few days later. Health Minister Ian Borg thanked the medical staff, including a surgeon who flew in for the procedure, and said the post-operative days are crucial with doctors closely monitoring the boys condition.

item.title: Maltese woman, 55, dies in traffic accident in Sicily
item.description: A 55-year-old Maltese woman died on Saturday afternoon after the car she was travelling in collided with a heavy goods vehicle near Modica, in Sicily. Italian media reported the crash occurred on the SS194 state road close to the coastal locality of Maganuco. The Italian police are investigating the circumstances.

item.title: Animal rights group flags dog breeder keeping dogs in a residential garage
item.description: Voice for the Animals has asked the authorities to act over allegations that a number of dogs kept in the garage of a private residence are mistreated, are used for breeding and that their pups are subsequently sold. The organisation said it has made several reports to the authorities responsible for animal welfare and published a video of the premises, noting that the allegations have not been independently confirmed. MaltaToday reported the same case, saying the video shows the owner occasionally coming out to the balcony to silence the dogs.

item.title: Maltese actor Peter Galea wins best actor award in Algeria
item.description: Peter Galea won the best actor award at the second edition of the Timimoun International Short Film Festival in Algeria for his performance in the Maltese short film Unur, Fama u Glorja, written and directed by Fabrizio Fenech. The prize was presented at the festivals closing ceremony on Tuesday 10 November in Timimoun. In the film he plays Pawlu, a boxing coach whose life changes drastically after his son falls into a coma. Galea has more than 20 years of experience across theatre, television and cinema and returned to Malta in 2001.

item.title: 85% of third-country nationals surveyed call Budget 2027 measures unfair
item.description: Eighty-five per cent of third-country nationals surveyed by Esprimi consider the Budget 2027 measures affecting them unfair and unnecessary, against just 20% of Maltese respondents. The survey of 122 non-EU residents, most without long-term residence status, found 46% unlikely to still be living in Malta in two years time. The measures welcomed least were the new 400 annual infrastructure contribution and higher work permit fees (71% each), the end of free childcare (68%) and the end of free public transport (57%).

item.title: Maltese crash victim in Sicily identified as Stephania Grech, 55
item.description: The Maltese woman killed in a collision with a trailer in Sicily has been identified as Stephania Grech, 55, who was travelling alone. Witnesses quoted by Italian media said Grech took a wrong turn emerging from a motorway junction on the SiracusaGela road near Modica, and the impact hurled her car some 60 metres from the point of collision; she died at the scene. The trailer driver, a 60-year-old man from Vittoria, was left in shock and Italian authorities are investigating.

item.title: Success of EU anti-cyberbullying app rests on member states, Micallefs Cabinet says
item.description: The success of the EUs planned online safety app for victims of cyberbullying will depend heavily on how national authorities adopt it, the Cabinet of Commissioner Glenn Micallef has said, with the Commission preparing to procure the tool next year. The app would let children and young people report cyberbullying to a helpline, securely store and transmit evidence and receive tailored support, and forms part of the Commissions Action Plan against cyberbullying, which contains 22 actions.

item.title: Animal Welfare Commissioner proposes noise limits for locally made fireworks
item.description: Animal Welfare Commissioner Elliot Magro has proposed scientifically determined noise limits for locally manufactured fireworks, buffer zones around animal farms and shelters, and advance notification of fireworks displays. The recommendations, presented to Parliamentary Secretary for Animal Welfare Alicia Bugeja Said, are aimed at closing gaps in the framework under the Control of Fireworks Act. Magro acknowledged fireworks are integral to Maltas village festas and said their preservation should be balanced with safeguards against unnecessary distress to animals.

item.title: Births to non-Maltese mothers risen from 24% to 37% of total since 2018
item.description: The share of births to non-Maltese mothers rose from 24.45% of total births in 2018 to 37.26% in 2025, figures obtained by The Malta Independent show. Births to Maltese mothers fell from 3,393 to 2,755 while births to non-Maltese mothers increased from 1,098 to 1,636, leaving the overall number of births broadly stable at 4,391. Adjusted for the population of women of reproductive age, the total fertility rate fell from 1.23 to 0.99, with Maltese women still recording a higher rate than non-Maltese women.

item.title: Public spending on energy and fuel subsidies has more than doubled in the past year
item.description: Government figures show electricity subsidies rising from 133.5 million in 2025 to a projected 290 million in 2026, while spending to sustain fuel subsidies is up from 38.7 million to 85 million. Total energy and fuel subsidies are projected at about 400 million this year, taking the amount spent since the schemes were introduced four years ago to 1.35 billion. The figures come from the governments pre-budget consultation document and are attributed to higher costs linked to the international situation.

item.title: 199 academics and education staff demand repeal of fee hikes for non-EU nationals
item.description: Almost 200 academics and education staff across Maltas post-secondary and tertiary institutions, including the University of Malta, MCAST, QMUL Malta and St Aloysius Sixth Form, have urged the government to repeal the Budget 2027 fee increases targeting third-country nationals. Signatories to a joint letter called the measures regressive and said the policy treats TCNs as indispensable economic engines while defining them as socially and civically disposable. The statement was issued ahead of the Green Ribbon week-long protest.

item.title: Climate change threatens Maltas tuna industry, 10-year plan warns
item.description: A proposed 10-year national aquaculture plan warns that rising sea temperatures could alter Atlantic bluefin tuna migration routes in the Mediterranean as early as 2030, threatening Maltas tuna fattening and export industry. The Action Plan for Sustainable Aquaculture 20262036, issued for public consultation, also flags higher risks of disease, parasites and mortality among captive tuna. The government proposes expanding fish farming further offshore and diversifying into new species while increasing production capacity.

item.title: Inquiry finds illegal electrical cable sparked the Salini fireworks factory blast
item.description: A magisterial inquiry into the 1 June explosion at the Ta Lourdes fireworks factory in Salini found that an illegal electrical cable, drawing power from a nearby farm under an informal arrangement in place for 26 years, ignited and set off a chain of blasts. Investigators estimated between eight and 11 tonnes of explosives were stored and manufactured irregularly on the site, with inspections failing to flag the breaches, and said a temporary extension lead buried in the ground had been installed in place of an armoured cable. The blast was felt kilometres away, damaged nearby homes and fields and destroyed the factory. The inquiry is expected to recommend criminal charges against several people.
